Subject: Post-incident compact and QBR readiness checkpoint — AtlasPay latency event

Team —

TL;DR: Attached is a 2-page compact postmortem for the AtlasPay tokenization latency event on 2027-03-28 (short spike in p95 from 180ms -> 1.2s; no data loss). I pulled the action roster and proposed a QBR slide deck outline that highlights customer impact, root cause, mitigations, and the ask for the execs.

Key items I need from this thread by EOD Friday:
- Confirm the three mitigations we surface in the QBR (short text, ownership, ETA).
- Approve the customer-facing summary for AtlasPay (one paragraph) to include in the customer-facing appendix.
- Sign off on the action tracker owners and whether we prioritize the hotfix vs. backlog refactor for the April sprint.

Attachments: 2027-04-01_postmortem_compact.docx (2 pages), incident_timeline_AtlasPay.xlsx (timeline + metrics)

Owners proposed in the doc:
- Short-term mitigation (fallback routing + throttling): Marissa Cole (target 2027-04-08)
- KV-cache tuning + quantization tweak: Rishi Malhotra (investigate by 2027-04-12)
- SLA guardrail (alert threshold & rollback policy): Laura Bennett (deliver SLO runbook draft by 2027-04-07)

Notes: Customer impact window and token counts are in the timeline spreadsheet. AtlasPay expects an updated ETA for remediation next week (they're on the QBR in two weeks). I tried to keep the compact to one page of executive bullets followed by a one-page action grid.

Thanks — please reply inline.

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference

1) Can we get a one-slide summary (PDF) that I can include in the exec packet? Focus on the customer impact (tokens affected, minutes of degraded perf), the immediate mitigation in-flight, and the residual SLA exposure (number).
2) Highlight the top three mitigations with clear trade-offs and whether they change cost profile materially (yes/no).

If Marissa and Rishi are comfortable with the dates above, I'll mark this as "QBR-ready" for the reliability section and confirm with sales leadership.

Subject: Re: Post-incident compact and QBR readiness checkpoint — AtlasPay latency event

Laura / team —

I've updated the action tracker and attached a CSV with owners, current status, and next steps. Short answers inline:

- Three mitigations to surface in QBR: (1) Fallback routing + short-term throttling (Marissa) — ETA 2027-04-08; (2) KV-cache tuning (Rishi) — ETA investigation complete 2027-04-12, PR target 2027-04-20; (3) SLA guardrail & alert tuning (Laura) — runbook draft 2027-04-07, rollout 2027-04-14.
- Cost impact: fallback/throttling = negligible; KV-cache tuning = slight memory bump on hosts (~+5%); longer-term refactor = moderate (TBD).
- Customer-facing paragraph (draft): "On March 28th we observed a brief latency spike affecting tokenization for a subset of AtlasPay traffic. No tokens were lost; our engineered fallback reduced request retries and we deployed a targeted throttling rule to restore p95 within 6 minutes. A prioritized action plan is in place and we will share post-QBR remediation milestones." Feel free to edit.

Attachments: action_tracker_AtlasPay.csv (owners/status), incident_timeline_AtlasPay.xlsx (updated)

I also built a one-slide PDF summary (saved to the drive link). If you want, I can produce a condensed 1-slide for the exec packet (ready by EOD tomorrow).

Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Sam Wells <sam.wells@atlaspay.com>

Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-incident compact and QBR readiness checkpoint — AtlasPay latency event

Thanks for the clear recap — appreciate the compact format. A few datapoints from our side to include in the QBR slide:

- Customer-observed impact window: 04:18–04:24 UTC on 2027-03-28.
- Estimated failed/slow tokenizations: ~1,200 (out of 1.1M requests that day).
- Business impact: Checkout conversion delta ~0.3% during the window (preliminary).

We'd like a firm ETA for the KV-cache tuning and an assurance the short-term throttling won't affect legitimate peak traffic patterns in next month's marketing push. Happy to join a 30-minute sync if helpful.

Regards,
Sam Wells
Director, Platform Ops — AtlasPay
sam.wells@atlaspay.com

Thanks all — good thread. Final plan and decisions:

1) QBR content: Marissa to produce the one-slide PDF (include customer-observed metrics that Sam supplied) by EOD Mon 2027-04-05. Vivek: I'll drop a one-paragraph exec note you can copy into the packet.
2) Mitigation priorities: short-term fallback + throttling (ship 2027-04-08) — proceed. KV-cache tuning (Rishi) — investigation complete 2027-04-12, plan + PR target 2027-04-20.
3) Customer communication: Approved draft paragraph for AtlasPay (Marissa's text) with one edit (clarify "no tokens lost" -> "no token data lost and no customer records affected"). Laura to send final customer note once runbook ETA confirmed.
4) QBR ask: We will request a 30-minute slot during the reliability portion to present (Vivek to confirm slot with Sales).

Open items (owners):
- Rishi: confirm memory delta and whether we need temporary instance sizing above baseline (due 2027-04-12).
- Marissa: finalize slide, attach the action tracker CSV in the packet (due 2027-04-05).
- Laura: finalize customer note & SLO runbook draft (due 2027-04-07).

Attachments: action_tracker_AtlasPay.csv (approved), incident_timeline_AtlasPay.xlsx (final).

I'll circulate the exec-slide PDF and a short speaking script tomorrow.
